title: Rolling-window token SLI prober and failover readiness canvas
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an instrumentation and visualization pipeline that combines a rolling-window, sequence-aware token SLI prober with a readiness canvas for multi-region failover and circuit breaker tuning. The goal is to provide per-tenant and per-shard SLO burn-rate surfaces tied to admission and fallback policies so SREs and oncall engineers can make informed progressive-shed decisions before incidents escalate.
background: We currently sample token latency at route-level and emit coarse p95/p99 aggregations. This obscures sequence effects, admission hysteresis, and tenant-driven burst behaviour that drive multi-region failovers and circuit trips. Existing dashboards are static and do not simulate progressive shedding or correlate KV cache hit rates with per-token costs. This ticket introduces: (1) a rolling-window token-level prober that preserves sequence boundaries, (2) adaptive sampling to prioritize long sequences and high-cost tenants, and (3) a dashboard canvas that surfaces failover readiness and admit policy effects over time.
deliverables: Rolling-window token SLI prober service (k8s job + lightweight worker) that emits token-level traces with sequence_id and admit_context
Adaptive sampling algorithm implementation (reservoir + weight by sequence length and tenant priority)
Failover readiness index metric: composite of regional availability, recent admit_rate, KV cache hit ratio, and circuit open probability
Grafana dashboard canvas with panels: sequence p50/p95/p99 token latency, admit rate heatmap, tenant burn-rate surface, circuit state timeline, simulated progressive-shed slider
Playbook section and runbook snippets for oncall: when readiness index < threshold trigger canary reroute, limit burst admission, or apply tenant-specific cap
Synthetic prober harness to validate dashboard signals (injectable into chaos testing)
Documentation and example queries for the data model (PromQL/Traces/ClickHouse examples)
E2E smoke tests and sampling correctness checks
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prober emits token-level spans that can be joined with admit events; 2) Sampling mechanism keeps memory bounded and preserves sequence-level statistics; 3) Dashboard renders <2s for pre-computed rollup queries and supports a 1h lookback by default; 4) Failover readiness index aligns with synthetic incident injections in >90% of runs; 5) Oncall playbook validated in runbook rehearsal.
implementation_notes:
- Use rolling-window aggregation (sliding window of 10m with 1m step) to compute sequence-aware SLI rollups.
- Sampler: reservoir sampling per-sequence with weights = min(1 + log(seq_len), 5) * tenant_priority_factor. Cap sampled tokens per-sequence to 256.
- Emit sampled traces to APM backend (trace_id includes sequence_id and shard_id). Emit derived metrics to TSDB: token_latency_bucketed, token_count_sampled, admit_event_rate.
- Pre-aggregate high-cardinality dimensions (tenant, shard) into hourly rollups in ClickHouse for dashboard fast-path.
- Dashboard should allow toggling between raw-sampled and rollup-derived panels.
- Progressive-shed simulator: client-side slider that manipulates admit_rate parameter and shows simulated impact on readiness index and projected SLO burn-rate.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
1) Sampling bias vs coverage: heavy weighting to long sequences improves detection of long-tail decode issues but risks underrepresenting short interactive sessions. We mitigate by ensuring minimum uniform sampling quota.
2) Cardinality explosion: per-tenant and per-route rollups can be large; mitigate with tiered rollups and only retaining top N tenants by spend for fine-grained panels.
3) Added telemetry cost: clickhouse storage and query costs will increase; propose budget alert and opt-in for low-tier tenants.
4) False positives in readiness index: synthetic validation and smoothing windows required to avoid flapping actions.
5) Complexity for oncall: provide simple threshold recommendations and default policies to avoid decision paralysis.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): deploy prober in us-west-2 and route 10% of sampled traffic; validate metrics and sampling correctness (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (regional expand): enable in primary regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1) and create per-region readiness index (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (dashboard and runbook): open dashboard to SRE/Platform and run two runbook rehearsals; collect feedback (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (wider rollout): enable sampling for all production routes with tenant opt-in for detailed rollups (3 weeks).
runbook_snippets: If readiness_index < 0.65 for >5m: escalate to SRE, enable canary reroute to secondary region and increase admission backpressure by 15% for best-effort tenants.
If p99 token latency increases 2x vs baseline and admit_rate drops >20%: check KV cache miss spike metric and recent kernel selection flags; consider rolling back recent runtime change.
If circuit_open_ratio > 0.2 on a shard: activate shard drain, reduce routed traffic, and notify customer success for affected tenants with high spend.
monitoring_queries_examples: ClickHouse sample: SELECT tenant, quantiles(0.5,0.95,0.99)(token_latency_ms) FROM token_sampled WHERE timestamp >= now()-toIntervalMinute(60) GROUP BY tenant
Trace join example: trace_id contains sequence_id; join trace spans with admit_event table on sequence_id to compute admit_latency_per_token
